{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Identify the six QA rows (revenue = 999999.99)
qa_rows = df[df['revenue'] == '999999.99']

# Confirm: these are 6 rows
assert len(qa_rows) == 6, f"Expected 6 QA rows, found {len(qa_rows)}"

# Check the status of these QA rows
qa_status_counts = qa_rows['status'].value_counts()
print(qa_status_counts)

# Total completed orders in the full dataset
total_completed_full = df['status'].value_counts().get('completed', 0)

# Since QA rows are not real orders, exclude them from the population
# But their status is not 'completed' (as shown by empty value_counts), so no adjustment needed
actual_completed = total_completed_full - qa_status_counts.get('completed', 0)

# Print the result
actual_completed"}
